To stay within supported versions and service-level agreements (SLA), upgrade to a supported version within 30 days after Azure removes version 1.34 Kubernetes Official version

0b1bf3f1-eb3e-4855-b9a5-06cde224c60d.recommendationDataSourceQuery:
Resources 
| where type =~ 'microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' 
| extend props = todynamic(properties) 
| mv-expand ap = props.agentPoolProfiles 
| extend currentOrchestratorVersion = tostring(ap.currentOrchestratorVersion) 
| extend requestedOrchestratorVersion = tostring(ap.orchestratorVersion) 
| extend orchestratorVersion = iff( 
    isempty(currentOrchestratorVersion), 
    requestedOrchestratorVersion, 
    currentOrchestratorVersion) 
| extend supportPlan = tostring(props.supportPlan) 
| where (orchestratorVersion == '1.34' 
    or orchestratorVersion startswith '1.34.') 
| where supportPlan =~ 'KubernetesOfficial' 
| project subscriptionId, id

actions.description: Upgrade AKS cluster to a supported Long Term Support Version

3afd0e0e-36bd-444b-97d7-d1e85d44066d.detailedDescription: Azure Kubernetes Service retires 1.30 LTS version. To stay within supported versions and service-level agreements (SLA), upgrade to a supported version within 30 days after Azure removes version 1.30 LTS.

3afd0e0e-36bd-444b-97d7-d1e85d44066d.recommendationDataSourceQuery:
Resources
 | where type =~ 'microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters'
 | extend props = todynamic(properties)
 | mv-expand ap = props.agentPoolProfiles
 | extend currentOrchestratorVersion = tostring(ap.currentOrchestratorVersion)
 | extend requestedOrchestratorVersion = tostring(ap.orchestratorVersion)
 | extend orchestratorVersion = iff(isempty(currentOrchestratorVersion), requestedOrchestratorVersion,
 currentOrchestratorVersion)
 | where orchestratorVersion == '1.30' or orchestratorVersion startswith '1.30.'
 | project subscriptionId, id

actions.caption: Change disk type
actions.description: Change disk type

3c03549b-9c0a-4c13-bed4-def3c7e34ddd.detailedDescription: HDD operating system (OS) disks are being retired in September 2028. Upgrade the OS disk from Standard HDD to Standard SSD for increased uptime of single-instance virtual machine and improved input/output operations and throughput.
3c03549b-9c0a-4c13-bed4-def3c7e34ddd.displayName: Upgrade to Standard SSD OS disk
3c03549b-9c0a-4c13-bed4-def3c7e34ddd.label: Upgrade to Standard SSD OS disk
3c03549b-9c0a-4c13-bed4-def3c7e34ddd.potentialBenefits: Boost single-instance VM uptime from 95% to 99.5%.
3c03549b-9c0a-4c13-bed4-def3c7e34ddd.recommendationDataSourceQuery:
resources
| where type =~ 'Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines'  
| extend provisioningState = tostring(properties.provisioningState)  
| extend creationTime = todatetime(properties.timeCreated)
| extend osDiskSKU = tostring(properties.storageProfile.osDisk.managedDisk.storageAccountType)
| extend isEphemeral = tostring(properties.storageProfile.osDisk.diffDiskSettings)
| extend runningState = tostring(properties.extended.instanceView.powerState.displayStatus)
| where provisioningState == "Succeeded"
| where osDiskSKU == "Standard_LRS"
| where isempty(isEphemeral)
| where creationTime < ago(7d) and creationTime > ago(8d)
| project subscriptionId, id

Resources 
| where type =~ 'microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' 
| extend props = todynamic(properties) 
| mv-expand ap = props.agentPoolProfiles 
| extend currentOrchestratorVersion = tostring(ap.currentOrchestratorVersion) 
| extend requestedOrchestratorVersion = tostring(ap.orchestratorVersion) 
| extend orchestratorVersion = iff( 
    isempty(currentOrchestratorVersion), 
    requestedOrchestratorVersion, 
    currentOrchestratorVersion) 
| extend supportPlan = tostring(props.supportPlan) 
| where (orchestratorVersion == '1.33'

| where supportPlan =~ 'AKSLongTermSupport' 
| project subscriptionId, id

actions.caption: Upgrade AKS cluster from 1.32 Kubernetes official version
actions.description: Upgrade AKS cluster from 1.32 Kubernetes official version

7dcef62e-792c-49dc-b36a-1938829c449c.detailedDescription: Azure Kubernetes Service retires 1.32 Kubernetes Official version. To stay within supported versions and service-level agreements (SLA), upgrade to a supported version within 30 days after Azure removes version 1.32 Kubernetes Official version
7dcef62e-792c-49dc-b36a-1938829c449c.displayName: Upgrade your AKS cluster from 1.32 Kubernetes Official version
7dcef62e-792c-49dc-b36a-1938829c449c.label: Upgrade your AKS cluster from 1.32 Kubernetes Official version
7dcef62e-792c-49dc-b36a-1938829c449c.recommendationDataSourceQuery:
Resources 
| where type =~ 'microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' 
| extend props = todynamic(properties) 
| mv-expand ap = props.agentPoolProfiles 
| extend currentOrchestratorVersion = tostring(ap.currentOrchestratorVersion) 
| extend requestedOrchestratorVersion = tostring(ap.orchestratorVersion) 
| extend orchestratorVersion = iff( 
    isempty(currentOrchestratorVersion), 
    requestedOrchestratorVersion, 
    currentOrchestratorVersion) 
| extend supportPlan = tostring(props.supportPlan) 
| where (orchestratorVersion == '1.32' 
    or orchestratorVersion startswith '1.32.') 
| where supportPlan =~ 'KubernetesOfficial' 
| project subscriptionId, id

Resources 
| where type =~ 'microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' 
| extend props = todynamic(properties) 
| mv-expand ap = props.agentPoolProfiles 
| extend currentOrchestratorVersion = tostring(ap.currentOrchestratorVersion) 
| extend requestedOrchestratorVersion = tostring(ap.orchestratorVersion) 
| extend orchestratorVersion = iff( 
    isempty(currentOrchestratorVersion), 
    requestedOrchestratorVersion, 
    currentOrchestratorVersion) 
| extend supportPlan = tostring(props.supportPlan) 
| where (orchestratorVersion == '1.34' 
    or orchestratorVersion startswith '1.34.') 
| where supportPlan =~ 'AKSLongTermSupport' 
| project subscriptionId, id

cc60a05a-1e40-403f-9790-28f310d54249.detailedDescription: Azure Kubernetes Service retires 1.37 LTS Kubernetes version. To stay within supported versions and service-level agreements (SLA), upgrade to a supported version within 30 days after Azure removes version 1.37 LTS Kubernetes version
cc60a05a-1e40-403f-9790-28f310d54249.displayName: Upgrade your AKS cluster from 1.37 LTS Kubernetes version
cc60a05a-1e40-403f-9790-28f310d54249.label: Upgrade your AKS cluster from 1.37 LTS Kubernetes version
cc60a05a-1e40-403f-9790-28f310d54249.recommendationDataSourceQuery:
Resources 
| where type =~ 'microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' 
| extend props = todynamic(properties) 
| mv-expand ap = props.agentPoolProfiles 
| extend currentOrchestratorVersion = tostring(ap.currentOrchestratorVersion) 
| extend requestedOrchestratorVersion = tostring(ap.orchestratorVersion) 
| extend orchestratorVersion = iff( 
    isempty(currentOrchestratorVersion), 
    requestedOrchestratorVersion, 
    currentOrchestratorVersion) 
| extend supportPlan = tostring(props.supportPlan) 
| where (orchestratorVersion == '1.37' 
    or orchestratorVersion startswith '1.37.') 
| where supportPlan =~ 'AKSLongTermSupport' 
| project subscriptionId, id

To stay within supported versions and service-level agreements (SLA), upgrade to a supported version within 30 days after Azure removes version 1.36 Kubernetes Official version
e828d5b8-b7bd-47b8-ac15-30e825ccdcfe.displayName: Upgrade your AKS cluster from 1.36 Kubernetes Official version
e828d5b8-b7bd-47b8-ac15-30e825ccdcfe.label: Upgrade your AKS cluster from 1.36 Kubernetes Official version
e828d5b8-b7bd-47b8-ac15-30e825ccdcfe.recommendationDataSourceQuery:
Resources 
| where type =~ 'microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' 
| extend props = todynamic(properties) 
| mv-expand ap = props.agentPoolProfiles 
| extend currentOrchestratorVersion = tostring(ap.currentOrchestratorVersion) 
| extend requestedOrchestratorVersion = tostring(ap.orchestratorVersion) 
| extend orchestratorVersion = iff( 
    isempty(currentOrchestratorVersion), 
    requestedOrchestratorVersion, 
    currentOrchestratorVersion) 
| extend supportPlan = tostring(props.supportPlan) 
| where (orchestratorVersion == '1.36' 
    or orchestratorVersion startswith '1.36.') 
| where supportPlan =~ 'KubernetesOfficial' 
| project subscriptionId, id

properties.description:
Service: Azure Managed Grafana

Region: West Europe

Stage: Planned

Impact category: Service Availability

You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that currently use Azure Managed Grafana.

Maintenance summary: This notification is for scheduled maintenance to your Azure Managed Grafana workspace(s) as part of a planned infrastructure upgrade. During the maintenance window, the affected workspace(s) will be temporarily unavailable, including dashboards, reports, and alerts. Full functionality will be restored once the maintenance is complete.

Maintenance date/time

  • Maintenance - Scheduled window: 1 October 2026 21:00 UTC to 2 October 2026 02:00 UTC
  • Expected duration of impact: Up to 30 minutes

Recommended action

No action is needed.

properties.description:
What happened?

Between 17:45 UTC and 18:46 UTC on 17 August 2026, a platform issue affected Azure Monitor in West Europe. Affected customers may have experienced intermittent failures when retrieving metric data for Azure Monitor workspaces or custom metrics. This included queries made through the Azure portal or programmatically through Azure Monitor APIs and Prometheus (PromQL) queries. Some metric alerts may not have activated as expected.


What went wrong, and why?

A software defect within one component of the metrics service, responsible for processing and serving customer metric data, caused the component to become unavailable. The issue occurred during an internal service reconfiguration, where the defect prevented the affected component from recovering as designed and significantly delayed its return to normal operation. As a result, the affected portion of the service remained unavailable for longer than expected, causing query failures for customers whose requests depended on the impacted metric data.

Under normal circumstances, the service would automatically transition workloads to healthy backup infrastructure to minimize customer impact. However, planned maintenance was simultaneously taking place on the infrastructure designated for automatic failover, preventing automatic recovery from completing as designed and requiring engineering intervention.

Once customer impact was confirmed, we paused the maintenance activity, verified the backup infrastructure was healthy, and manually transitioned the workload to restore service. Once the transition was complete, affected customer metric queries returned to normal operation.


How did we respond?

  • 17:45 UTC on 17 August 2026 - Customer impact began.
  • 18:02 UTC on 17 August 2026 - Internal service telemetry detected elevated failure rates, and engineers began investigating.
  • 18:17 UTC on 17 August 2026 - The system determined that the outage criteria had been met, declared an outage, and sent initial communications to impacted customers.
  • 18:45 UTC on 17 August 2026 - After confirming the health of alternate capacity, engineers initiated a service failover to move query traffic away from the affected capacity.
  • 18:46 UTC on 17 August 2026 - Query availability returned to expected levels, and customer impact ended.


How are we making incidents like this less likely or less impactful?

  • We have optimized the affected component's recovery process, to improve recovery times and reduce the duration of impact during similar service events. (Completed)
  • We have improved our instrumentation related to background processing, to accelerate detection and diagnosis of similar issues in the future. (Completed)
  • We have updated our troubleshooting procedures, to improve identification of process blocking conditions and to provide faster mitigation guidance for engineers responding to similar events. (Completed)
  • We are optimizing our internal recovery operations, to reduce the amount of time required for affected service components to return to normal operation following service reconfiguration activities. (Estimated completion: November 2026)


How can customers make incidents like this less impactful?

  • Consider reviewing Azure multi-region design patterns and guidance for regions and availability zones when designing critical workloads: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/architecture/patterns/geodes and https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/well-architected/design-guides/regions-availability-zones 
  • Consider evaluating the reliability of your applications using guidance from the Azure Well-Architected Framework and its interactive Well-Architected Review: https://aka.ms/AzPIR/WAF 
  • The impact times above represent the full incident duration and are not specific to any individual customer. Actual impact varied between customers and resources. For guidance on implementing monitoring to understand granular impact, refer to https://aka.ms/AzPIR/Monitoring
  • Consider ensuring that the right people in your organization receive notifications about future service issues by configuring Azure Service Health alerts: https://aka.ms/AzPIR/Alerts


How can we make our incident communications more useful?

updates.summary:
What happened?

Between 17:45 UTC and 18:46 UTC on 17 August 2026, a platform issue affected Azure Monitor in West Europe. Affected customers may have experienced intermittent failures when retrieving metric data for Azure Monitor workspaces or custom metrics. This included queries made through the Azure portal or programmatically through Azure Monitor APIs and Prometheus (PromQL) queries. Some metric alerts may not have activated as expected.


What went wrong, and why?

A software defect within one component of the metrics service, responsible for processing and serving customer metric data, caused the component to become unavailable. The issue occurred during an internal service reconfiguration, where the defect prevented the affected component from recovering as designed and significantly delayed its return to normal operation. As a result, the affected portion of the service remained unavailable for longer than expected, causing query failures for customers whose requests depended on the impacted metric data.

Under normal circumstances, the service would automatically transition workloads to healthy backup infrastructure to minimize customer impact. However, planned maintenance was simultaneously taking place on the infrastructure designated for automatic failover, preventing automatic recovery from completing as designed and requiring engineering intervention.

Once customer impact was confirmed, we paused the maintenance activity, verified the backup infrastructure was healthy, and manually transitioned the workload to restore service. Once the transition was complete, affected customer metric queries returned to normal operation.


How did we respond?

  • 17:45 UTC on 17 August 2026 - Customer impact began.
  • 18:02 UTC on 17 August 2026 - Internal service telemetry detected elevated failure rates, and engineers began investigating.
  • 18:17 UTC on 17 August 2026 - The system determined that the outage criteria had been met, declared an outage, and sent initial communications to impacted customers.
  • 18:45 UTC on 17 August 2026 - After confirming the health of alternate capacity, engineers initiated a service failover to move query traffic away from the affected capacity.
  • 18:46 UTC on 17 August 2026 - Query availability returned to expected levels, and customer impact ended.


How are we making incidents like this less likely or less impactful?

  • We have optimized the affected component's recovery process, to improve recovery times and reduce the duration of impact during similar service events. (Completed)
  • We have improved our instrumentation related to background processing, to accelerate detection and diagnosis of similar issues in the future. (Completed)
  • We have updated our troubleshooting procedures, to improve identification of process blocking conditions and to provide faster mitigation guidance for engineers responding to similar events. (Completed)
  • We are optimizing our internal recovery operations, to reduce the amount of time required for affected service components to return to normal operation following service reconfiguration activities. (Estimated completion: November 2026)


How can customers make incidents like this less impactful?

  • Consider reviewing Azure multi-region design patterns and guidance for regions and availability zones when designing critical workloads: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/architecture/patterns/geodes and https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/well-architected/design-guides/regions-availability-zones 
  • Consider evaluating the reliability of your applications using guidance from the Azure Well-Architected Framework and its interactive Well-Architected Review: https://aka.ms/AzPIR/WAF 
  • The impact times above represent the full incident duration and are not specific to any individual customer. Actual impact varied between customers and resources. For guidance on implementing monitoring to understand granular impact, refer to https://aka.ms/AzPIR/Monitoring
  • Consider ensuring that the right people in your organization receive notifications about future service issues by configuring Azure Service Health alerts: https://aka.ms/AzPIR/Alerts

properties.description:
You’re receiving this notification because one or more Azure subscriptions associated with your account use Microsoft Marketplace Windows Server 2022 images. You can also find this notification in the Azure portal under Service Health > Health advisories by using tracking ID 8PJS-_48. 

In October 2024, we announced upcoming changes to Microsoft Marketplace Windows Server 2022 images. On 14 July 2026, we deprecated images preinstalled with .NET 6 because .NET 6 had reached the end of support. To avoid disruptions, migrate any affected SKUs listed below to supported Windows Server 2022 images. Use the new offer ID (Offer ID) provided in the linked announcement. 

  • 2022-DATACENTER 
  • 2022-DATACENTER-AZURE-EDITION 
  • 2022-DATACENTER-AZURE-EDITION-CORE 
  • 2022-DATACENTER-AZURE-EDITION-CORE-SMALLDISK 
  • 2022-DATACENTER-AZURE-EDITION-HOTPATCH 
  • 2022-DATACENTER-AZURE-EDITION-HOTPATCH-SMALLDISK 
  • 2022-DATACENTER-AZURE-EDITION-SMALLDISK 
  • 2022-DATACENTER-CORE 
  • 2022-DATACENTER-CORE-G2 
  • 2022-DATACENTER-CORE-SMALLDISK 
  • 2022-DATACENTER-CORE-SMALLDISK-G2 
  • 2022-DATACENTER-G2 
  • 2022-DATACENTER-SMALLDISK 
  • 2022-DATACENTER-SMALLDISK-G2 

Recommended action 

To avoid disruptions, migrate affected workloads to supported Microsoft Marketplace Windows Server 2022 images now. Review the .NET 6 image migration guidance to learn how to identify affected images in your subscriptions, complete the migration, and locate the replacement images. 

Help and support 

If you have questions or encounter issues related to the end of support for .NET 6 or migration to a supported version, visit the Services Hub or create an Azure support request. When creating the request, select the product family Developer Tools, the product .NET, and the version .NET 10.

Impact Statement: Starting at 19:00 UTC on 08 September 2026, you have been identified as a potentially impacted customer using the Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) service who may experience a black screen when users attempt to launch an AVD session when using FSLogix. Impacted customers may encounter this issue if their AVD host has the September Windows update installed, KB5124008 (2609B) on Windows Server and/or Windows client-multisession.


Current Status: We detected this issue via customer reports indicating the black screen they encounter when attempting to launch AVD sessions. We are aware of this issue and are actively investigating to fully understand the specific change introduced in the September Windows update that contributed to the issues.

We are actively collaborating across multiple teams and resources to finalize determination of appropriate mitigation measures. While this remains ongoing, we are continuously monitoring the situation while working to ensure full-service restoration.

The next update will be provided on 24 September 2026, or sooner as events warrant.

properties.description:
What happened?

Between 17:45 UTC and 18:46 UTC on 17 August 2026, a platform issue affected Azure Monitor in West Europe. Affected customers may have experienced intermittent failures when retrieving metric data for Azure Monitor workspaces or custom metrics. This included queries made through the Azure portal or programmatically through Azure Monitor APIs and Prometheus (PromQL) queries. Some metric alerts may not have activated as expected.


What went wrong, and why?

A software defect within one component of the metrics service, responsible for processing and serving customer metric data, caused the component to become unavailable. The issue occurred during an internal service reconfiguration, where the defect prevented the affected component from recovering as designed and significantly delayed its return to normal operation. As a result, the affected portion of the service remained unavailable for longer than expected, causing query failures for customers whose requests depended on the impacted metric data.

Under normal circumstances, the service would automatically transition workloads to healthy backup infrastructure to minimize customer impact. However, planned maintenance was simultaneously taking place on the infrastructure designated for automatic failover, preventing automatic recovery from completing as designed and requiring engineering intervention.

Once customer impact was confirmed, we paused the maintenance activity, verified the backup infrastructure was healthy, and manually transitioned the workload to restore service. Once the transition was complete, affected customer metric queries returned to normal operation.


How did we respond?

  • 17:45 UTC on 17 August 2026 - Customer impact began.
  • 18:02 UTC on 17 August 2026 - Internal service telemetry detected elevated failure rates, and engineers began investigating.
  • 18:17 UTC on 17 August 2026 - The system determined that the outage criteria had been met, declared an outage, and sent initial communications to impacted customers.
  • 18:45 UTC on 17 August 2026 - After confirming the health of alternate capacity, engineers initiated a service failover to move query traffic away from the affected capacity.
  • 18:46 UTC on 17 August 2026 - Query availability returned to expected levels, and customer impact ended.


How are we making incidents like this less likely or less impactful?

  • We have optimized the affected component's recovery process, to improve recovery times and reduce the duration of impact during similar service events. (Completed)
  • We have improved our instrumentation related to background processing, to accelerate detection and diagnosis of similar issues in the future. (Completed)
  • We have updated our troubleshooting procedures, to improve identification of process blocking conditions and to provide faster mitigation guidance for engineers responding to similar events. (Completed)
  • We are optimizing our internal recovery operations, to reduce the amount of time required for affected service components to return to normal operation following service reconfiguration activities. (Estimated completion: November 2026)


How can customers make incidents like this less impactful?

  • Consider reviewing Azure multi-region design patterns and guidance for regions and availability zones when designing critical workloads: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/architecture/patterns/geodes and https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/well-architected/design-guides/regions-availability-zones 
  • Consider evaluating the reliability of your applications using guidance from the Azure Well-Architected Framework and its interactive Well-Architected Review: https://aka.ms/AzPIR/WAF 
  • The impact times above represent the full incident duration and are not specific to any individual customer. Actual impact varied between customers and resources. For guidance on implementing monitoring to understand granular impact, refer to https://aka.ms/AzPIR/Monitoring
  • Consider ensuring that the right people in your organization receive notifications about future service issues by configuring Azure Service Health alerts: https://aka.ms/AzPIR/Alerts


How can we make our incident communications more useful?

You can rate this PIR and provide any feedback using our quick 3-question survey: https://aka.ms/AzPIR/TJGB-WGG

properties.description:
Service: Azure Managed Grafana

Region: West Europe

Stage: Planned

Impact category: Service Availability

You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that currently use Azure Managed Grafana.

Maintenance summary: This notification is for scheduled maintenance to your Azure Managed Grafana workspace(s) as part of a planned infrastructure upgrade. During the maintenance window, the affected workspace(s) will be temporarily unavailable, including dashboards, reports, and alerts. Full functionality will be restored once the maintenance is complete.

Maintenance date/time

  • Maintenance - Scheduled window: 1 October 2026 21:00 UTC to 2 October 2026 02:00 UTC
  • Expected duration of impact: Up to 30 minutes

Recommended action

No action is needed.

To view the list of Affected Resources, go to the 'Impacted Resources' tab of this event within Service Health/Planned Maintenance tab in the Azure portal. For this event, the provided list is a 'static' snapshot of impacted resources at the time this notification was published. We also recommend configuring service health alerts for increased visibility into notices for your subscription.

Help and support

If you have questions, get answers to your technical questions and issues from community experts in Microsoft Q&A or open a ticket for Azure Managed Grafana. If you have a support plan and need technical help, you may also create a support request.

properties.description:
Service: Azure Managed Grafana

Region: West Europe

Stage: Planned

Impact category: Service Availability

You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that currently use Azure Managed Grafana.

Maintenance summary: This notification is for scheduled maintenance to your Azure Managed Grafana workspace(s) as part of a planned infrastructure upgrade. During the maintenance window, the affected workspace(s) will be temporarily unavailable, including dashboards, reports, and alerts. Full functionality will be restored once the maintenance is complete.

Maintenance date/time

  • Maintenance - Scheduled window: 2 October 2026 21:00 UTC to 3 October 2026 02:00 UTC
  • Expected duration of impact: Up to 30 minutes

Recommended action

No action is needed.

To view the list of Affected Resources, go to the 'Impacted Resources' tab of this event within Service Health/Planned Maintenance tab in the Azure portal. For this event, the provided list is a 'static' snapshot of impacted resources at the time this notification was published. We also recommend configuring service health alerts for increased visibility into notices for your subscription.

Help and support

If you have questions, get answers to your technical questions and issues from community experts in Microsoft Q&A or open a ticket for Azure Managed Grafana. If you have a support plan and need technical help, you may also create a support request.

updates.summary:
This notification is for previously scheduled maintenance to your Azure App Service instance(s) in Italy North. The maintenance has now completed. During this time, your Azure App Service application(s) may have seen a brief drop in connectivity for a few seconds. Please see frequently asked questions for maintenance notifications: Routine maintenance for App Service. For maximum availability and minimal disruption to your service, follow our list of best practices outlined here: The Ultimate Guide to Running Healthy Apps in the Cloud. Feel free to refer to your Azure portal for more information, FAQs regarding routine maintenance notifications, and for any additional questions, please contact support.
